module_title: Advanced Analysis - LPG Reforms, Narasimham Committee, and Mega-Mergers
introduction: This level analyzes the drastic shifts in the banking sector post the 1991 Economic Reforms and the recent historic 'Mega-Consolidations' executed by the government to create global-sized Public Sector Banks (PSBs). Today, only 12 PSBs remain.

core_concepts.title: Narasimham Committee (1991 & 1998)
core_concepts.description: Known as the 'Father of Banking Reforms in India'. Post the 1991 crisis, based on this committee's recommendations, the RBI issued licenses to 'New Generation Private Banks' (like HDFC, ICICI, Axis), ending the monopoly of nationalized banks. The committee also heavily recommended the merger of weak banks and lowering the CRR/SLR.

core_concepts.title: Merger of SBI Associates (2017)
core_concepts.description: The State Bank of India had 5 associate banks (e.g., State Bank of Bikaner & Jaipur, Hyderabad, etc.) and one Bharatiya Mahila Bank (BMB). On April 1, 2017, all of these were formally merged into the parent SBI, instantly catapulting SBI into the list of the top 50 largest banks globally.

core_concepts.title: Mega-Mergers of PSBs (2019-2020)
core_concepts.description:
To strengthen balance sheets and create global competitive banks, the government aggressively consolidated PSBs: 
1. Vijaya Bank + Dena Bank = Bank of Baroda (2019). 
2. Oriental Bank of Commerce (OBC) + United Bank of India = Punjab National Bank (PNB). 
3. Syndicate Bank = Canara Bank. 
4. Allahabad Bank = Indian Bank. 
5. Andhra Bank + Corporation Bank = Union Bank of India.

core_concepts.title: Current Status (The Final 12)
core_concepts.description: In 2017, India had 27 Public Sector Banks. Following all the mega-mergers, the total number of PSBs in India has currently dropped to exactly '12'. (SBI is the largest, followed by PNB, and then Bank of Baroda).

important_entities.name: Mission Indradhanush (2015)
important_entities.significance: A comprehensive 7-point action plan (A to G) launched by the Government of India to reform the functioning of PSBs and tackle the massive mounting problem of NPAs (Non-Performing Assets). (A-Appointments, B-Bank Board Bureau, C-Capitalization...).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not confuse Mergers with Privatization. When Allahabad Bank was merged into 'Indian Bank', it did not become private; it simply became a part of a larger 100% government-owned Public Sector Bank.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: PNB has OU, Canara has Syn, Indian has Allah
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: PNB = OBC + United. Canara = Syndicate. Indian Bank = Allahabad. (This solves almost all 'Match the Following' questions on this topic).

exam_strategy_tips: Current Affairs Economics: The most frequently asked question regarding this topic today is 'How many Public Sector Banks (PSBs) currently exist in India?' The answer is 12.
